title: UNESCO Sites in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has three World Heritage properties, not three buildings.** Museum Island, the Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin, and the Berlin Modernism Housing Estates, which alone spread across seven separate addresses.

**The list grew on 26 July 2026.** The UNESCO Committee, meeting in Busan, added the Waldsiedlung Zehlendorf as the seventh modernism estate. Bruno Taut, Hugo Häring and Otto Rudolf Salvisberg built its 1,917 homes in a pine forest between 1926 and 1932.
**Only one is in the centre.** Museum Island is three minutes from Alexanderplatz on the U5, and it is the one World Heritage site my free tour walks through.

**Five of the seven estates are ordinary residential streets.** People live there. You walk the pavement, look up, and leave. That is the whole visit, and it is worth knowing before you spend fifty minutes getting to one.

**If you make one trip out, make it the Hufeisensiedlung in Britz.** Twenty-two minutes on the U7 to Parchimer Allee, a horseshoe of flats around a pond, and the only estate with resident-led guided tours.

**Pair the two northern estates.** Bristolstraße at the Schillerpark estate and Aroser Allee at the Weiße Stadt are three minutes apart on the 120 bus, so doing one without the other wastes the journey.
**Everything on the list is inside the city boundary,** so an AB ticket covers all of it, including the Wannsee palaces.
